outcome: conditions of childbirth (conversion to cesarean section, postpartum blood loss)
duration of labor (first, second, third stages, total duration)
umbilical artery blood gas analysis indices (pH, arterial carbon dioxide partial pressure, arterial oxygen partial pressure, arterial hydrogen ion concentration)
stress indices (nitric oxide, cortisol, adrenaline levels)
cohort: A total of 120 women giving natural birth at Changning District Maternal and Child Health Hospital between December 2021 to December 2022.
finding: Combined spinal-epidural anesthesia effectively reduced anxiety, provided labor analgesia, shortened the second and third stages of labor, and lowered postoperative stress levels without causing significant motor block compared to epidural anesthesia.
mod_finding: The rates of conversion to cesarean section were lower in the combined spinal-epidural anesthesia group compared to the epidural anesthesia group.
